The best university for nursing in the world is the University of Pennsylvania, based on the latest QS subject ranking for Nursing. King’s College London ranks second globally and remains the strongest nursing university in the UK.

That gives you the ranking answer.

But here’s the thing: the best nursing school on a ranking table is not always the best choice for every student. A student planning to work in the NHS may look closely at UK nursing universities. Someone aiming for US nursing registration may care more about NCLEX preparation, programme accreditation and state licensing. A Canadian applicant may compare province, clinical placements and local registration routes.

Fees matter too. So does language, scholarship availability, intake timing and the country where you want to practise after graduation.

This guide compares the best universities for nursing in the world for 2027. You will see the latest ranking picture, what each top nursing school is known for, how costs differ by country, and what international students should check before applying.

How to read nursing rankings properly

A ranking tells you which universities perform strongly in reputation, research and subject-level indicators. It does not tell you whether that university is right for your budget, licence route or career country.

Nursing is different from many subjects. You are not only choosing a university; you are choosing a professional pathway.

A strong nursing university should offer recognised nursing programmes, clinical placement opportunities, academic support, credible research and a clear route towards professional registration in the country where you want to practise.

Factor

Why it matters

Ranking and reputation

Helps you identify globally recognised nursing schools

Accreditation or registration route

Nursing is regulated, so the degree must match the country’s rules

Clinical placements

Nursing is not classroom-only; practice experience matters

Tuition and living cost

Intake timing

Some courses fill early, and not every nursing course offers January or May entry

Career destination

The best country to study nursing is often the country where you want to work

A mildly surprising point: the “best” nursing school may be wrong for you if it sits in the wrong licensing system. A student who wants to become a registered nurse in the UK should not choose a US school only because it ranks higher globally.

Top nursing schools in the world: what each one is best for

1. University of Pennsylvania, USA

The University of Pennsylvania ranks first in the latest available QS Nursing subject ranking. Penn Nursing has a long reputation for research, leadership and advanced nursing education.

It is a strong option for students who want a research-driven nursing environment in the United States. The school is also known for graduate study, leadership pathways and links with major healthcare systems.

For international students, the biggest question is cost. Penn’s latest published undergraduate tuition and fees are $73,978 for 2026–27 before wider cost-of-attendance items. For 2027 entry, check the updated fee before budgeting, along with scholarships, living costs and the licensing route.

Best for: research-focused students, future nursing leaders and students targeting the US healthcare route.

2. King’s College London, UK

King’s College London ranks second globally and first in the UK in the latest available QS Nursing ranking. It remains one of the most recognised names for nursing education in the UK.

King’s is especially relevant for students who want to study nursing in the UK and understand the NHS environment. Its Florence Nightingale Faculty of Nursing, Midwifery & Palliative Care has a strong international reputation, and the university sits in a major healthcare city.

For students considering the UK route, check the official NMC approved programmes list before applying. That matters more than ranking alone. If your goal is UK registration, the course must match the correct professional route.

If the UK is your target, it is safer to understand UK course types, NMC approval and fees first before comparing university names.

Best for: UK nursing route, NHS-focused students, research and clinical learning.

3. Johns Hopkins University, USA

Johns Hopkins is a major name in health sciences and nursing education. Its nursing school is particularly strong for students looking at graduate-entry nursing, public health, research and clinical innovation.

One reason Johns Hopkins attracts global attention is its Entry into Nursing route for students who already hold a bachelor’s degree in another field. That route can suit career changers, but it is intensive.

Best for: graduate-entry nursing, US nursing route, public health and clinical leadership.

4. University of Toronto, Canada

The University of Toronto is one of Canada’s strongest nursing universities. Its Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing is known for research, accelerated nursing education and links with the Canadian healthcare system.

The BScN route is especially useful for students with previous university study. Toronto’s tuition and fees page currently lists 2025–26 international BScN Year 1 fees at CA$55,142.92. Students planning 2027 entry should check the updated fee before budgeting.

If Canada is your target country, look beyond ranking. Province, registration, clinical placements, tuition and post-study route all matter. Before choosing a province, look at the Canadian route and compare it with your long-term plan.

Best for: Canadian nursing route, accelerated BScN, research and healthcare systems study.

5. Duke University, USA

Duke University School of Nursing is one of the strongest US nursing schools and ranks fifth in the latest available QS Nursing ranking. It is often associated with advanced nursing, clinical education and healthcare leadership.

Duke may be more relevant for students looking at graduate or advanced nursing routes than for students who simply want the cheapest undergraduate nursing option. The USA offers excellent training, but cost and licensing can be complex.

In the USA, accreditation also matters. The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education explains that CCNE reviews the quality and integrity of baccalaureate, graduate and residency or fellowship programmes in nursing.

Best for: advanced nursing, US clinical education, leadership and graduate study.

6. National University of Singapore, Singapore

The National University of Singapore is tied sixth in the latest available QS Nursing ranking. It is one of Asia’s strongest names for healthcare education and research.

NUS can be a strong choice for students who want a leading Asian university with regional and international reputation. Still, nursing is practical and regulated. Check language expectations, clinical placement structure and whether the route matches where you want to practise.

Best for: Asia-focused nursing study, healthcare research and students comparing Singapore with the UK, USA, Canada or Australia.

7. The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong

The Chinese University of Hong Kong is also tied sixth in the latest QS Nursing ranking. Its Nethersole School of Nursing is one of Asia’s strongest nursing schools and a major name in the region.

Hong Kong may appeal to students who want high-quality nursing education closer to Asia, with strong research and clinical connections. As with every country, check language, registration and career route before deciding.

Best for: Asian nursing education, research and regional healthcare careers.

8. Columbia University, USA

Columbia University School of Nursing ranks eighth in the latest available QS Nursing ranking. It is a strong US name, especially for graduate nursing, advanced practice and healthcare leadership.

International students should check programme level carefully. Columbia may not be the right option for someone searching only for a basic low-cost nursing degree, but it can be highly relevant for students aiming at advanced practice or graduate nursing in the USA.

Best for: graduate nursing, advanced practice and students targeting the US healthcare system.

9. University of Alberta, Canada

The University of Alberta ranks ninth in the latest available QS Nursing ranking and remains one of Canada’s strongest nursing names.

It may be useful for students who want a Canadian route outside Toronto. That can matter because tuition, living costs, clinical exposure and province-based registration planning may differ across Canada.

If Canada is your main destination, do not compare universities by ranking alone. Compare province, programme type, tuition and registration route together.

Best for: Canadian nursing, healthcare research and students comparing more than one province.

10. University of Manchester, UK

The University of Manchester is tied tenth in the latest available QS Nursing ranking and remains a strong UK option for nursing and healthcare education.

Manchester can be a practical alternative for students who want a strong UK university outside London. That may help with living-cost planning, although tuition, placements and NMC approval still need checking.

If your long-term plan is the UK, start with the professional route. A recognised name helps, but an NMC-approved course is the key.

Best for: UK nursing study, clinical learning and students comparing outside-London options.

10. Trinity College Dublin, Ireland

Trinity College Dublin is tied tenth in the latest available QS Nursing ranking and is one of Europe’s respected names for nursing and midwifery education.

Ireland may interest students who want an English-speaking European study destination. But you still need to check registration rules, clinical route, fees and post-study work options before applying.

Best for: European nursing, English-speaking study, clinical and research-led education.

Best universities for nursing by country

A global ranking is useful, but many students choose by country first. That is sensible. Nursing is tied to local healthcare systems and professional registration.

Best nursing schools in the USA

The USA has several of the world’s top nursing schools, including the University of Pennsylvania, Johns Hopkins, Duke, Columbia and others. US nursing education can be excellent, but it can also be expensive.

Students should check programme type, accreditation, NCLEX preparation, state licensing route, clinical placements, scholarships and total cost. A high-ranking school is only useful if the programme matches the route you want.

Best nursing universities in the UK

The UK is strong for students who want structured nursing routes, clinical placements and an NHS-linked pathway. King’s College London and the University of Manchester remain in the latest QS top group, while other universities may be stronger depending on nursing field and course type.

UK applicants must check NMC approval. This is not optional. A course can sound impressive, but if it does not match the right professional registration route, it may not take you where you want to go.

Students who are still comparing the UK with other destinations can also review the broader UK study route before making a nursing shortlist.

Best nursing schools in Canada

Canada remains popular for healthcare education, respected universities and post-study opportunities. The University of Toronto and University of Alberta both appear strongly in the latest available QS Nursing ranking.

For Canada, check the province, registration route, course type, international tuition, clinical placement model and post-study work rules. A Toronto-based course and an Alberta-based course may both be excellent, but the local route can feel different once you start planning registration and cost.

Best nursing universities in Asia

Asia has strong nursing education options, especially in Singapore and Hong Kong. NUS and CUHK both sit inside the latest available QS Nursing top group.

For students from Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan, Nigeria or Ghana, Asia may feel closer and more familiar. Still, recognition, clinical language, registration and career destination matter.

Best nursing universities in Australia

Australia does not dominate this QS top 10 list in the same way as the USA or UK, but it remains a popular nursing destination for international students.

Before choosing Australia, check registration with Ahpra and the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Fees, English requirements and placement expectations can vary widely. If Australia is on your list, compare the Australian study route before committing.

What about India, Nigeria, the Philippines and Indonesia?

Many students from India, Nigeria, the Philippines and Indonesia search for the best nursing schools in the world because they are comparing more than a university name. They are comparing migration route, cost, recognition and whether the degree can support their career in another country.

For these students, the safest shortlist usually starts with three questions: where do you want to register as a nurse, what can you afford without depending on uncertain scholarships, and does the university clearly explain clinical placement and professional requirements?

That is why a student from India may compare Canada, the UK and the USA differently from a student from Nigeria. A student from the Philippines may already understand nursing as an exportable career path, but still needs to check licensing rules country by country. An Indonesian applicant may care more about language, cost and regional access.

So yes, ranking matters. But fit matters more.

Here is a practical example. A student from Bangladesh with school-level qualifications may not need Penn or Johns Hopkins first. A three-year UK BSc Nursing route could be more realistic. A graduate from India with a life science degree may compare accelerated routes in the USA, Canada or UK. A student already planning to work in Canada should not ignore province-based registration.

That is the real decision.

When should you apply for nursing intakes?

Nursing courses can be more time-sensitive than many classroom-based degrees because universities may need interviews, health checks, placement planning and professional approval checks.

A safer timeline looks like this:

Intake goal

What to do

September intake

Start shortlisting 9–12 months earlier where possible

January intake

Check availability early because nursing options can be limited

May intake

Treat it as course-specific, not guaranteed

Next academic year

If you are comparing UK dates, start with nursing courses in the UK for 2027, then check January intake options and May intake availability before planning your timeline.

Admission requirements for top nursing universities

Admission requirements vary by country and programme, but most top nursing schools look for academic strength, communication skills and evidence that you understand healthcare practice.

Requirement

What it usually means

Academic qualification

School results, previous degree or prerequisite courses

English language

IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or accepted alternatives

Prerequisites

Biology, chemistry, maths or social science may be required

Personal statement

Your motivation and understanding of nursing

Interview

Common for nursing and healthcare programmes

Health and character checks

Often required before placements

Registration pathway

You must understand the route in your target country

A strong applicant does not just say, “I want to help people.” That is too easy. A better applicant explains what they have seen, learnt or done. Maybe they volunteered at a clinic. Maybe they cared for a family member. Maybe they shadowed a nurse and realised how much communication matters during stressful moments.

Small real examples make a nursing application more believable. If you are struggling with that part, turn your care experience into a stronger nursing statement before submitting applications.

Ranking vs real fit: how to choose the right nursing university

Rankings matter. They help you find respected institutions. But nursing is not like choosing a general business degree.

A top nursing university should fit your professional goal.

Ask yourself:

  • Where do I want to work after graduation?
  • Does this degree support that country’s registration route?
  • Can I afford the full cost, not just tuition?
  • Will I study in a language I can use in clinical practice?
  • Does the course include enough placement experience?
  • Is this undergraduate, graduate-entry or advanced nursing?
  • What happens after graduation?

The short answer is this: choose the university that connects ranking, registration, cost and career. If one part does not fit, the ranking alone will not save the decision.

There is no single best country to study nursing for every student. Each destination has a different advantage.

For many international students, the best country is the one where they can afford the degree, complete clinical training, meet registration rules and realistically work after graduation.

When you are still comparing destinations, compare the country route before choosing a university.

FAQs about the best universities for nursing in the world

What is the best university for nursing in the world?

The University of Pennsylvania ranks first in the latest available QS World University Rankings by Subject for Nursing, published in 2026. King’s College London ranks second globally.

What are the best universities for nursing?

The best universities for nursing include the University of Pennsylvania, King’s College London, Johns Hopkins University, University of Toronto, Duke University, National University of Singapore, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Columbia University, University of Alberta, University of Manchester and Trinity College Dublin.

What are the top nursing schools in the world?

Top nursing schools include the University of Pennsylvania, King’s College London, Johns Hopkins University, University of Toronto, Duke University, National University of Singapore, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Columbia University, University of Alberta, University of Manchester and Trinity College Dublin.

Is UPenn or King’s College London better for nursing?

UPenn ranks first in the latest QS Nursing ranking, while King’s College London ranks second and is first in the UK. UPenn may suit students targeting the US route, while King’s may suit students focused on UK nursing and NHS-linked education.

Which country is best for studying nursing?

The best country depends on your career plan. The USA is strong for elite research and advanced nursing, the UK is strong for NHS-linked training, Canada has respected healthcare education, and Singapore or Hong Kong may suit students looking at strong Asian healthcare systems.

Are the best nursing schools expensive?

Many top nursing schools are expensive, especially in the USA and Canada. Penn currently lists 2026–27 tuition and fees at $73,978, while Toronto’s nursing page lists 2025–26 international BScN Year 1 fees at CA$55,142.92.

Which nursing school is best for international students?

When should I apply for nursing intakes?

For September intake, start as early as possible because nursing courses may need interviews, health checks and placement planning. January and May intakes can exist, but nursing availability is course-specific and should not be assumed.

What should I check before choosing a nursing university?

Do rankings matter for nursing?

Rankings matter, but they should not be your only factor. Nursing is a regulated profession, so the degree must also fit the licensing or registration system in your target country.

Which UK university is best for nursing?

King’s College London is the top UK university in the latest available QS Nursing ranking and ranks second globally. The University of Manchester also appears in the latest QS top group.

Which nursing schools are good for graduate-entry students?

Johns Hopkins, University of Toronto and some UK universities may offer graduate-entry or accelerated nursing routes. Always check whether the programme is designed for students who already hold a degree.

Final advice before you apply

Start with the ranking, but do not stop there.

The best universities for nursing in the world can give you reputation, research strength and strong clinical exposure. Still, your final choice should match your budget, country plan, intake timing, licensing route and long-term career goal.

A top-ranked nursing school is valuable only if it gets you closer to the nurse you want to become.

If the name is impressive but the route does not fit, keep looking.
